assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuinely new quantum behaviour in a material: a purely geometric twist tunes flat bands and yields correlated insulators and superconductivity in a carbon-only system. It echoes the graphene lesson that experiment can overturn what theorists thought, and it opened the whole moire-materials field. A continuum band-structure prediction followed by direct experimental realization is the theory-meets-measurement story I value.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model supplied the magic-angle prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group delivered the decisive 2018 experiments. Two laureates is a clean configuration; Bistritzer, then a postdoc, is a possible but less natural third.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated phases and superconductivity, and the interpretation is still developing but the core phenomenon is stable. Recognition is timely, with a few years of consolidation behind it.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility
Fair credit relative to other early theory and to fabrication-technique pioneers is not fully clear to me

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT is the workhorse theory for strongly correlated electrons and explains the Mott transition and the evolution of spectra in real materials, particularly in combination with DFT. It sits squarely in my own area and has changed how correlated materials are computed and compared with spectroscopy. Originality and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar made the mapping onto a quantum impurity problem and the practical framework. The three credited names cover the core, but Metzner is not in the credited list and I cannot propose him; the omission is a real fairness concern within the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use, benchmarking against experiment and extensions such as DFT+DMFT make this mature, and recognition is arguably overdue. It is a theory method rather than a single discovery, which some colleagues may weigh differently.
uncertainties: Credit omission of Metzner and others who developed solvers and extensions
Whether a method qualifies as a discovery in the sense of the statutes
Quantitative accuracy for materials with strong non-local correlations is limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect revealed a new class of electronic states, with protected surface or edge conduction set by band topology rather than symmetry breaking. Theory predicted it and experiments confirmed it in HgTe, and first-principles calculations helped identify materials. Very high originality and field-wide influence.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall idea; Molenkamp's group gave the HgTe experimental demonstration following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. A theory-plus-experiment trio is natural, though Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and others (and Haldane's earlier 2016 recognition of topological phases) complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups and materials, including 3D topological insulators, and well established over nearly two decades. Timely and mature, though the 2016 prize covers part of the conceptual ground.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 topological-phase prize and with the 3D topological insulator discoveries by others
Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not in the credited list
Applications remain limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the MgO magnetic tunnel junction are a landmark in spin-dependent transport, rooted in band-structure and symmetry filtering of tunnelling states, and underpin hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It connects magnetism theory, which I know well, with a major device impact, and it follows naturally from the 2007 GMR prize.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in amorphous alumina junctions in 1995, and Parkin and the Yuasa group demonstrated giant TMR in epitaxial MgO. The credited trio covers the discovery and the MgO engineering. Theoretical predictions by Butler, Mathon and others and Yuasa's experiments are not in the supplied credit, which leaves the configuration open.
assessment.maturity: Long confirmed, widely deployed commercially and well understood theoretically through first-principles calculations. Recognition is timely or even somewhat late.
uncertainties: Allocation between alumina TMR and MgO coherent tunnelling
Theory and epitaxial MgO contributors are outside the credited names
Possible view that this is mainly engineering after GMR

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, giving direct access to the superfluid-Mott transition and to many-body physics that is hard to compute. It is a new quantum-simulation tool with clear connections to the condensed-matter problems I work on. I would still want the discovery to be defined precisely.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and co-workers proposed the Bose-Hubbard realization, with Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger giving the key experiments on the Mott transition and the fermionic Hubbard simulations. Greiner is part of the experimental core, so choosing three of the four names needs discussion.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of confirmation across many labs, and the interpretation is stable. Quantum gas microscopy is still evolving, but recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Which of Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger should be selected for the Mott transition
Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and neighbouring AMO prizes
Whether quantum simulation yields new physical knowledge beyond the platform

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum anomalous Hall effect gives quantized Hall conductance with no external field, in a magnetic topological insulator, and thus links magnetism, topology and electronic structure. The theory proposal used first-principles calculations of Cr- or Fe-doped materials, a methodology I trust, and the experimental realization was a hard materials-physics achievement.
assessment.attribution: Fang and Dai and collaborators proposed the magnetic topological insulator route and Xue's group delivered the 2013 observation; the credited trio fits that story. The earlier Haldane model and other contributors (for example Yu et al. in Science 2010) are not credited, so fairness depends on how those are weighed.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by several groups, but quantization is only at low temperature and has been difficult to extend, so the maturity is lower than for the quantum Hall effect itself. Timing is probably a bit early.
uncertainties: Low temperature of the quantization and sample homogeneity
Independence of early confirmations
Credit relative to Haldane and other theorists

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built from Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's implementation at record precision, opened a new regime of frequency metrology with reach to tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The importance is high, although my expertise in AMO is more limited than in condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice trapping and Ye's group pushed it to the quantum many-body regime and record accuracy, so the pair is a natural and fairly clean two-person configuration. Others working on single-ion clocks have been recognised in 2012 or are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmation across several national laboratories and consistent progress make this mature; timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock-related prizes (Hall and Hansch in 2005, Wineland in 2012)
Whether Ye is also best placed under a thorium-229 nuclear-clock candidate
I defer to colleagues with AMO expertise

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intrinsic magnetism in atomically thin crystals such as CrI3 and Cr2Ge2Te6 shows that long-range order survives in the two-dimensional limit once anisotropy is present, which refines the Mermin-Wagner expectation. It also ties into my own work on 2D magnets and into new spintronic materials. A clear, verified discovery sits at the centre.
assessment.attribution: The 2017 monolayer CrI3 magneto-optic work by Xu's group and the Cr2Ge2Te6 bilayer work associated with Zhang's group are the decisive reports; Jarillo-Herrero's group did related tunnelling work later. I would credit two experimentalists, but the relative weight of near-simultaneous papers is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed and extended by many groups, but the field is only about nine years old and applications are still emerging, so this is probably premature compared with the candidates above.
uncertainties: Premature relative to established candidates
Simultaneous and related discoveries complicate attribution
Technological relevance not yet demonstrated
